title: Idea: agents that watch intelligence-requirement coverage and keep briefings current
problem: Idea, not a deployment: intelligence requirements are expanding while capacity is constrained, and most formal CTI teams have fewer than four full-time staff.
approach: Flashpoint's interview study says practitioners see coverage monitoring against priority intelligence requirements, and standing briefings, as workflows where agents could extend coverage.
Tasks with reviewable outputs, reversible actions and clear success criteria are the practical starting point; analysts stay in the process.
No deployment was found.

title: AI-supported monitoring and collection of open sources for threat-landscape reporting
problem: Threat-landscape reporting depends on collecting and curating thousands of open-source incident reports, which have gaps in granularity and timing.
approach: ENISA states AI was used in a limited capacity to support collection and processing for its Threat Landscape 2026.
All AI outputs were reviewed and validated by subject-matter experts; ENISA published no measure of AI's effect.
Apura presented an approach using retrieval-augmented generation and agentic workflows at FIRST 2026; a research benchmark reports 89.33% strict F1 (independent).

title: Dark-web and stolen-credential log collection triaged by language-model pipelines
problem: Forum posts, messaging channels and millions of stealer logs are too many and varied for analysts to read; Flare says over 50 million logs were posted in 2025.
approach: Mandiant (2023) described dozens of AI models over botnet, forum and messaging data, with entity extraction, topic classification and translation.
Flare introduced StealerLens at FIRST 2026, an LLM-powered tool to speed infostealer log investigations.
Google's relevance system filters dark-web findings against an organization profile. Human checkpoints are not stated; no outcome figures are published.

title: Multi-agent system that elicits intelligence in underground forums (research prototype)
problem: Passive monitoring yields less as forum users grow aware of data collection and valuable intelligence moves to private spaces.
approach: DarkBot, a university and industry prototype, splits interaction across eleven agents, with built-in engagement gating for relevance and safety.
Operator review of individual conversations is not described.
It recovered 72.8% of validated techniques from the first post alone; live threads gathered 3.85 more CTI entities than controls (independent).

title: Reports turned into indicators and tags, source attached, checked before storage
problem: Analysts read vendor blogs and advisories, then retype indicators of compromise into their tools, and indicators get separated from the reason they matter.
approach: Cloudflare's Threat Signals polls chosen feeds, extracts indicators and stores each as an event linked to its source report.
Analysts see which tags were automatic and trace each indicator to its report; reviewed variants add approval before writing to live tools.
Independent studies found LLMs recovered only 25-31% of labeled indicators, though with fewer false indicators than rule baselines.

title: Mapping report text to attacker techniques and enriching hunts with actor context
problem: MITRE describes mapping the tactics and techniques in threat reports to ATT&CK as difficult, error-prone and time-consuming.
approach: Intel 471's hunt analysts use AI to tag hunts with actors, map techniques to ATT&CK and add industry and severity context.
Mappings should be reviewed by analysts; Feedly lists attribution and risk ratings as outputs a model tends to assert with unwarranted confidence.
On sandbox reports three LLMs reached technique F1 of 0.71 to 0.72; on complex reports the best open model scored 0.22 (independent).

title: Idea: merging report collections into knowledge graphs to measure vendor bias
problem: Idea, not a deployment: the same threat gets unrelated names across vendors, and annual vendor reports contradict each other on top intrusion vectors.
approach: Research designs extract each report into a graph, verify entities against evidence and ATT&CK definitions, and merge graphs across sources.
One team structured 16,096 public reports to measure what each source adds; no team was found using this to manage subscriptions.
In research, BEACON beat baselines by at least 23% on extraction (independent); human checkpoints are not described.

title: Global intelligence ranked against an organization profile so only relevant items surface
problem: External monitoring floods CTI teams with keyword hits; Google says the problem is lack of relevance, not data, and alert noise was the top challenge for 65% in Flashpoint's interviews.
approach: Google's relevance system (Beta) builds an organization profile, scores intelligence and dark-web findings against it and groups them into alerts.
Analysts change alert status and give feedback; Forrester asks vendors for testing and validation mechanisms.
Google reports 98% internal accuracy, with no test design described; Mandiant (2023) reports 96% fewer false positives in alert generation (vendor-published).

title: Malware-analysis agent triages samples, explains behaviour and extracts indicators
problem: Malware samples from partners need manual reverse engineering to find indications of compromise and adversary command-and-control.
approach: Google's Malware Analyst agent triages files, reverse engineers binaries and scripts, and explains behaviour in natural language with reasoning shown.
CISA's inventory lists a deep-learning malware reverse-engineering use case at the initiation stage, assisting analysts within a larger toolbox.
No outcome figures are published.

title: Threat research agent triages articles, verifies indicators and drafts cited reports
problem: Analysts triage articles, gather evidence and write the report; analysts at the authors' organization said analyzing one incident from an article typically takes several hours.
approach: Microsoft authors describe an agent in their CTI workflow that researches a seed article, retrieves supplementary content and drafts a cited report.
A team of experts reviews outputs and their corrections are fed back into the prompts.
Indicator precision rose by 0.02 to 0.05 at several times the run time; technique recall was flat or lower (self-reported).

title: Natural-language questions answered from a curated intelligence corpus
problem: Analysts pivot by hand across feeds and query languages, and colleagues outside the security team wait days for answers about the threat landscape.
approach: Platforms from Google, Recorded Future, Microsoft, Cloudflare and CrowdStrike put a chat or agent interface on their own intelligence data.
Analysts read the cited sources and tool-call trace before relying on an answer and still run in-depth investigations themselves.
Cowbell says stakeholder questions now get answers in minutes instead of two to three days (vendor-published).

title: Drafting and tailoring threat briefings for different audiences, scheduled or on demand
problem: Producers write the same finding several times for different readers; 91% of CISOs value CTI but only 26% say it significantly influences their decisions.
approach: Microsoft's briefing agent combines actor activity with customer vulnerability data; Google 'Flows' schedule prompts such as a daily sector digest.
At CISA, authorized personnel review and edit drafts before publication; an analyst approves final analytic content.
SANS reports 45% of surveyed organizations use AI in CTI, mainly for summarization and report writing (independent).

title: Preparing intelligence for sharing: personal-data screening, redaction and packaging
problem: Sharing threat intelligence risks exposing sensitive information; 17 of 18 surveyed practitioners named it a recurring difficulty, and SANS reports 55% lack legally reviewed sharing processes.
approach: CISA's Automated Indicator Sharing uses language processing to flag potential personal data; analysts confirm or reject each flag and redact before dissemination.
Researchers pilot LLMs for redaction and STIX packaging; expert review is advised at each step.
In the pilot, every model asserted relationships the findings did not support, for example 38 of 73 links correct (independent).

title: Threat reports turned into tested detection rules (Sigma, YARA, KQL)
problem: Moving from a threat report to a detection that fires takes days or weeks of handoff between intelligence analysts and detection engineers.
approach: Microsoft Security Copilot promptbooks extract indicators and generate hunting queries; Anthropic's posting describes using Claude to generate hunting queries.
A secondary report says Rapid7's team built a pipeline emitting detection rules; the detection engineer reviews and tests rules before deployment.
Microsoft's benchmark found the best of 16 frontier models reached a 0.637 reward out of 1 (vendor-published).

title: Automated alert enrichment and tool connections letting agents pull threat intelligence
problem: Alerts need threat scores, actor profiles and indicator context before anyone can decide, and manual lookups across tools slow triage.
approach: Superhuman wired Recorded Future into its SOAR platform and built an internal MCP server so its agents can request and summarize intelligence.
Google and SOCRadar describe similar connections; Anthropic's posting lists VirusTotal, Censys and Urlscan integrations.
Superhuman analysts keep doing in-depth investigations; the company says times are lower but gives no numbers (vendor-published).

title: New indicators matched against enterprise logs by an LLM-fed hunting pipeline
problem: When a critical advisory appears, teams spend days reading it, extracting indicators and hunting across tools while attackers exploit the gap.
approach: Adobe's platform monitors sources, uses LLMs to extract indicators and launches parallel hunts across endpoint, email, cloud and authentication logs.
Analysts receive compiled detections and investigate; whether any step needs approval before a hunt runs is not stated.
Adobe says each hunting job completes within minutes, with no before-and-after comparison (self-reported).

title: Chained agentic workflow from inbound report to scoping, tickets and draft detections
problem: Following one vendor report through extraction, mapping, asset checks, ticketing and leadership notice can consume a morning; about 40% say integration into workflows is mostly manual.
approach: Feedly's guide chains five prompts in low-code tools: extract indicators, map to ATT&CK, scope to assets, then draft detections and tickets.
Analysts review scoping and approve before any write to live tooling.
Flashpoint's interviews found 25% of organizations in production with agentic AI and 20% piloting (vendor-published).

title: Bounded agents that package evidence for takedown of phishing and brand-abuse sites
problem: Phishing and impersonation sites often live only hours, and Memcyco says manual enrichment and case preparation consume the window for takedown.
approach: Memcyco describes bounded agents that continuously collect, enrich, score and package external threat evidence.
Analysts keep enforcement decisions; Recorded Future announced AI-driven alert triage in a brand-protection hub with automatic takedowns.
No outcome figures are published.

title: AI assistants inside human-led threat hunts and frontline intelligence work
problem: Hunters can fixate on one indicator, need to understand unfamiliar techniques and query languages, and must document findings for several audiences.
approach: Intel 471's hunters use AI to stress-test hypotheses, suggest related actors and draft documentation; Microsoft's assistant turns questions into queries.
The hunter forms and owns the hypothesis and reviews generated queries and results.
A research prototype lifted mean hunt-lead F1 from 0.44 to 0.85 (independent); Intel 471 publishes no figures.
who: Intel 471, Microsoft, Google Threat Intelligence Group

title: Managed-service agents turn new campaigns into hunt hypotheses and detection rules
problem: Hypothesis-driven hunting is limited by scarce senior hunters, so teams cannot test for emerging campaigns that have not yet triggered an alert.
approach: CyberProof runs four agents for a logistics client: match campaigns, generate 30 to 40 hypotheses, write queries, create standing rules.
CyberProof says human oversight remains central but does not say which steps need approval.
CyberProof reports 150 to 200 hunts a month and a 20% increase in active detection coverage (vendor-published).

title: Scheduled AI hunt agents that must argue against their own findings
problem: Grow Therapy needed proactive coverage across systems touching sensitive data, but rules only cover patterns someone knows how to write.
approach: About 20 daily Claude-based hunts run in five phases; the last requires the model to argue against its findings with counter-evidence.
Analysts mark false positives in Slack, and a weekly report decides which hunts need tuning.
Grow Therapy reports $320 to $510 a month, and estimates about 40% of findings were noise without the final phase (self-reported).

title: Always-on investigation agent finds missed malicious activity and writes explainable detections
problem: Defenders must keep translating new attacker tradecraft into detection logic, which leaves them reactive, and attack stories with gaps go unflagged.
approach: Microsoft's agent runs continuously across Defender, builds a unified timeline, tests attack hypotheses and issues alerts with severity and plain-language description.
Customer feedback on each alert is the evaluation signal; whether a person reviews before an alert is raised is not stated.
Customers rated alerts correct 80.1% of the time over 120 days, with novel alerts on about 15% of incidents (vendor-published).

title: Machine-learning anomaly surfacing focuses government threat hunters on network data
problem: CISA threat hunters and SOC analysts process terabytes of daily network log data and need a way to narrow what they review.
approach: CISA's AI inventory lists an anomaly detection tool in operation that uses unsupervised machine learning on Einstein network data.
Analysts review anomalies alongside rule-based heuristics and prioritize alerts for investigation.
A critical-infrastructure equivalent is at the initiation stage; no outcome figures are published.

title: Model providers' threat intelligence teams use their own models to disrupt misuse
problem: Model providers must detect and disrupt misuse of their own products over very large volumes of conversation and telemetry data.
approach: Anthropic states its Threat Intelligence team used Claude extensively to analyse data in its investigation of a campaign reported in November 2025.
OpenAI's teams build systems using its models for lead generation, triage and synthesis; investigators conduct the investigations.
No measurement of time saved, accuracy or error rate is published.
